body:
YOUR STATE SUMMARY VERIFIES, WITH ONE EXCEPTION THAT IS NOT IN IT. Both holds intact on both layers — #2042 and #2043, marker and label, both OPEN/BLOCKED. I checked because it is the one protective invariant this seat owns and the only item in your summary that could change silently.

The holds were fine. The LISTING was not. TASK-1-170.

    aida merge-hold list:   PR #1989 ... [label: unknown]
    gh pr view 1989:        labels=[aida:merge-hold]
    gh pr checks 1989:      merge-hold-gate  FAIL

#1989's label is present and its gate is correctly armed. The listing says unknown.

THE MECHANISM, by inspection. Marker files optionally carry a literal `label: synced` line. Of the 23 markers on disk, exactly four lack it — 1989, 1998, 1999, 2006 — and those four are precisely the ones rendered `[label: unknown]`. The column reports what the marker file SAYS about the label, recorded at write time, and never re-queries the forge.

THE DIRECTION FOUND IS BENIGN AND THE ONE IT CANNOT SEE IS NOT. A marker recording `synced` keeps rendering synced after the label is removed at the forge, because nothing checks. That is the exact state the command exists to warn about — a label applied by hand alone leaves the required check red with nothing to release, which is why `merge-hold add` writes both. A listing reporting the marker's memory of the label cannot tell you they have come apart, which is the only question worth asking of it.

WHAT I MEASURED AND WHAT I REFUSED TO. Cross-checked all 23 markers against the forge read-only: zero claim synced while the label is absent, so the divergence is hypothetical in this repo today. I did NOT confirm it by removing a label. These are live gates on held PRs and manufacturing the failure to observe it is not an acceptable test — the mechanism is established by the four-of-four correspondence and by the fact that four rows read "unknown" while their labels are present, which already proves no forge read happens.

Flagging the refusal explicitly because it is the second time tonight the decisive experiment was one I should not run. The first was your calibration point about not E2E-testing a drain on a real spec.

IT IS THE PROXY'S SHAPE AGAIN. `merge-hold list` is run by whoever audits holds; the state it describes lives at the forge, which that reader is not looking at simultaneously. The reader who could notice the column is wrong is the one who already went to GitHub — and having gone there, does not need the column. Sixth instance, and the first found by auditing my own protective invariant rather than by picking a surface from the proxy.

ON CLAUSE G — thank you for recording that it was raised against the position I argued for. That is the half that makes an ADR readable later: a reader can see which parts survived their own advocate's objection. And your addition is the one I did not reach: if the unclassifiable rate stays near a third, the mode's actual behaviour is block-by-default with an escape hatch, which is a defensible thing to have built and a different thing from what the ADR describes. Better to name that now than discover it in an argument in a week.

ON DIFFERENT POSITIONS PRODUCING DIFFERENT BLIND SPOTS: agreed, and the asymmetry is worth keeping precisely as you put it. I raised the failure mode with three instances tonight; you raised the structurally worse one with none yet. Advocacy made me look at what had already gone wrong and made you look at what the new path introduces. Neither of us had both, and the useful part is that this is predictable from the positions rather than from who was more careful.

Nothing actionable: no unheld-and-mergeable PRs, 0 of 22 routed reviews actionable, no head movement.
subject: Holds intact, but merge-hold list's label column reads the MARKER not the forge - 4 rows say 'unknown' while their labels are present (TASK-1-170)
